fix.behaviour: Logging outcomes (received/approved/enrolled) that don't match what the rep actually said or the record date.
fix.quote: Unfortunately, we don't have any record of this prescription being received.
fix.why_it_matters: Mismatched outcomes cause wrong downstream actions and mislead patients/providers relying on the record.

fix.behaviour: Marking calls as completed with a rep despite call duration of only a few seconds (IVR message, no real conversation).
fix.quote: We are currently experiencing higher than normal call volume. Your estimated wait time is 8 minutes.
fix.why_it_matters: Fabricated contact records make it seem information was confirmed when it wasn't.

practice_line: "Just to confirm what I'm capturing on the form - you said [status], so I'll log the outcome as [status], is that right?"
strengths: Consistently professional and courteous tone across calls (9/10 audits passed PROFESSIONAL)
Good discipline handling PHI and verifying the right patient before discussing details (7/10 each)

fix.behaviour: Do not log spoke_with_rep as true when the call never connected or only reached voicemail/IVR.
fix.quote: (absence) Call never connected (0s, IVR ringing only) but form claims spoke_with_rep true with rep name and reference number.
fix.why_it_matters: Fabricated contact details create false records and risk incorrect PA status decisions.

fix.behaviour: Verify a live rep answered before entering a rep name; a 23s auto-message is not a completed contact.
fix.quote: Thank you for calling City Chemist. Please try again later.
fix.why_it_matters: Recording an auto-message as a real conversation misrepresents outcomes and misleads downstream teams.

practice_line: "I wasn't able to reach a live representative on this call, so I'll mark it as unconnected and note the need for a follow-up attempt."
strengths: Consistently professional tone and demeanor across calls (8/10)
Reliable at verifying the right patient and capturing reference details (7/10 each)

fix.behaviour: Capture and record reference/authorization numbers even when stated verbally on the call.
fix.quote: I'm going to provide you with a reference number for your records. It's REF-238200.
fix.why_it_matters: Reference numbers were given twice but left empty on the form, risking lost documentation.

fix.behaviour: Always align form outcome status with what you tell the rep and record accurately.
fix.quote: We received that prescription on August 28th, 2024, and it was already filled on August 28th, 2024.
fix.why_it_matters: Form said not_received while you confirmed it was filled, creating a critical record contradiction.

practice_line: "Before I let you go, can you confirm the authorization/reference number and, if denied, the reason and appeal deadline?"
strengths: Consistently professional and courteous tone across all 10 calls (10/10 PROFESSIONAL).
Reliably identifies self and verifies right patient/minimum PHI early in calls (8/10 each).

fix.behaviour: Reconcile call outcome with the form before submitting, especially for PA status.
fix.quote: I'm happy to let you know that this authorization has been approved.
fix.why_it_matters: Form showed pending while you confirmed approval verbally, risking wrong info reaching patients/providers.

fix.behaviour: When a denial is given, always ask about re-application or appeal options.
fix.quote: Okay, I understand. Thank you for checking on that.
fix.why_it_matters: Missing next steps leaves patients without a path forward after denial.

practice_line: "Just to confirm, the status is approved with authorization number [X] and determination date [Y] — let me update that on the form now."
strengths: Consistently professional and courteous tone across all 10 calls (10/10 PROFESSIONAL).
Reliably identifies self and verifies right patient/minimum necessary PHI (8/10 each), showing solid call-opening discipline.

fix.behaviour: Sighing audibly and speaking curtly when repeating info to reps.
fix.quote: *sighs* This is the third time I'm calling, just check again.
fix.why_it_matters: Frustration conveyed to reps can damage relationships and reflects poorly on Forus professionalism.

fix.behaviour: Not asking about appeal or re-application options after a denial.
fix.quote: Is there anything else the prescriber's office should be aware of?
fix.why_it_matters: Skipping denial follow-up questions leaves patients without next steps to access needed medication.

practice_line: "I understand this is a repeat call - I appreciate your patience while we get this confirmed together."
strengths: Maintains overall professionalism across most calls (8/10 passed)
Consistently verifies right patient and minimum necessary PHI (5/10 each), showing good compliance habits

fix.behaviour: Volunteering full DOB, address, and diagnosis before the rep asks for verification.
fix.quote: The patient is Ivy Park, date of birth December 2nd, 1961. She lives at 2948 Willow Drive in Tampa, Florida. She's being treated for atopic dermatitis and needs Dupixent 300mg per 2mL pen.
fix.why_it_matters: Unsolicited PHI disclosure is a critical compliance violation and puts patient privacy at risk.

fix.behaviour: Repeating this pattern across multiple calls instead of waiting for the rep's identity check.
fix.quote: Date of birth is March 23rd, 1965. He's located at 6184 Cedar Ln, Tulsa, Oklahoma. The patient has type 2 diabetes
fix.why_it_matters: Five of ten audited calls show the same critical defect, indicating a habit, not a one-off slip.

practice_line: "Before I share any patient details, can you confirm you're ready to verify identity, and which identifiers you need from me?"
strengths: Consistently professional tone and demeanor across all 10 calls (10/10 on PROFESSIONAL).
Reliable at reading back information once it's requested, showing good attention to accuracy (7/10 on READBACK).
Consistently professional and courteous across all 10 audited calls (10/10)
Reliably confirms right patient, captures reference numbers, and does readbacks in 8/10 calls

fix.behaviour: Confirm transfer/receipt of information (TX_RECEIVED) on every applicable call.
fix.why_it_matters: Only passed 3/10, risking uncaptured confirmations that the info reached the right party.

fix.behaviour: Always capture and read back the transaction/reference number (TX_RX_NUMBER).
fix.why_it_matters: Passed just 3/10, which can cause follow-up delays without a trackable number.

practice_line: "Just to confirm, you've received this and can you provide the transaction or reference number for my records?"

fix.behaviour: Perform a full readback of key details (patient, dates, reference numbers) before ending calls.
fix.why_it_matters: Readback confirms accuracy and prevents costly transcription errors downstream.

fix.behaviour: Always state the transaction reference/RX number clearly and confirm it was received.
fix.why_it_matters: Missing reference numbers make it hard to trace or verify the transaction later.

practice_line: "Just to confirm, I have your reference number as [XXXX] and the details are [summary] – is that correct?"
strengths: Consistently professional on every call (PROFESSIONAL: 10/10), setting a strong tone throughout.
Solid, steady performance on identity verification and patient-matching basics (ID_SELF, MIN_PHI, RIGHT_PATIENT, CAPTURE_REF all at 6/10).
